parameters.note: Overall product width, outer faces of the side panels.
Overall product height from the floor, plinth included.
Overall outer depth: back panel + carcass + front door gap + door (ADR-003). Without doors: back + carcass.
auto = minimum section count that keeps each section inner width <= maxShelfSpanMm.
Carcass, partition and plinth board. Its thickness drives all carcass geometry (replaces D-0 panelThickness). Decors themselves are unconfirmed placeholders (catalog).
'same_as_corpus' = door decor follows corpusMaterial. Door thickness = this material's thickness.
Assumed: HDF back nailed over the carcass back (overlay). Material and thickness = constants.backMaterial (catalog).
Assumed: plinth by default; 'none' = carcass bottom directly on the floor (no legs in v0).
Assumed plinth height range and default. Used only when base = plinth.
Assumed: setback of the front plinth strip from the carcass front edge. Back strip is never recessed.
Preset for all sections. auto: single door if the single-leaf width (coverage minus gaps) <= maxSingleLeafWidthMm, else double. Hinges follow the hinge rule (ADR-006).
Staff override for section 1. 'preset' = follow the doors preset. Ignored if the wardrobe has fewer sections.
Staff override for section 2. 'preset' = follow the doors preset. Ignored if the wardrobe has fewer sections.
Staff override for section 3. 'preset' = follow the doors preset. Ignored if the wardrobe has fewer sections.
Staff override for section 4. 'preset' = follow the doors preset. Ignored if the wardrobe has fewer sections.

maxShelfSpanMm.note: Assumed maximum section inner width before shelves sag (SHELF_SPAN warning, sections=auto).

backMaterial.note: Assumed back panel material (catalog id). Its thickness is the back thickness.

doorGapFrontMm.note: Assumed gap between the carcass front edge and the back face of the overlay door.

doorGapBetweenMm.note: Assumed gap between two adjacent door leaves.

doorGapEdgeMm.note: Assumed gap between a door leaf and the outer carcass edge (left, right, top, bottom). Also used next to a section without a door.

maxSingleLeafWidthMm.note: Assumed maximum width of one door leaf. Single source for doors=auto (single vs double) and DOOR_TOO_WIDE; measured on the leaf, not the section opening.

doorLeafRoundingMm.note: Assumed rounding step for door leaf widths; the remainder goes to the leaves that lost most by rounding so leaves + gaps = covered width exactly.

maxDoorHeightMm.note: Assumed door height above which DOOR_TOO_HEIGHT warns (warping risk).

constructionRules.note: Side panels run the full carcass height and stand on the plinth (carcass height = height - plinthHeight).
Top and bottom are fitted between the side panels (length = width - 2 x panelThickness).
Sections share the inner width equally in whole millimetres; any remainder (< sections mm) goes +1 mm to the leftmost sections.
Plinth = front and back strips, full product width, board thickness = panelThickness. Front strip set back by plinthRecess, back strip flush with the carcass back. No side returns in v0.
Vertical partitions are fitted between top and bottom and run the full carcass depth.
depth = back + carcass + (doors ? doorGapFront + door : 0). carcassDepth = depth - back - (doors ? door + doorGapFront : 0). Decided in D-1a (ADR-003).
The overlay back covers the carcass only (width x carcass height), not the plinth.
The front plinth strip is set back from the carcass front (not from the door) by plinthRecess.
Doors are overlay (nakladnye): they cover the carcass front. Height = carcass height - 2 x doorGapEdge; the plinth stays visible.

Door coverage of a section ends at the centre line of its partitions (outer carcass edge for the end sections); a double door splits its coverage in two leaves. Leaf widths are rounded to doorLeafRoundingMm (ADR-006).

Decided in D-1b (ADR-006): no two leaves hinge on the same partition. Per run of doored sections the pattern is L* D? R* (at most one double); free singles: first max(1, floor(m/2)) left, rest right — 1: L, 2: L,R, 3: L,R,R, 4: L,L,R,R. A staff override that breaks it is a HINGE_CONFLICT error.

sections=auto picks the smallest count that keeps every section inner width <= maxShelfSpanMm AND, when the doors preset is not none, gives a door layout without DOOR_TOO_WIDE / HINGE_CONFLICT (e.g. 1360 mm with doors=auto -> 3 sections, because 2 sections would need two adjacent double doors).
